summary: This function scans a directory recursively to find all files, counts them by file extension while skipping common ignored folders like .git and node_modules, then generates and prints a Mermaid pie chart showing the distribution of file types in the project.

explanations.7: Path is being used instead of os.path because it provides a more modern, object-oriented way to work with file paths that works consistently across Windows and Unix systems.
explanations.9: This set defines folder names that should be completely ignored during the scan—things like version control directories and package caches that clutter the statistics.
explanations.12: rglob('*') recursively searches the directory and all subdirectories, returning every file and folder it finds.
explanations.13: This checks two things: that the item is actually a file (not a folder), and that none of the folder names in its path are in our ignored list—if any ignored folder is in the path, we skip it entirely.
explanations.14: If the file has an extension (the part after the dot), convert it to lowercase; otherwise, use the string 'No extension' as a placeholder.
explanations.17: Counter tallies up how many times each extension appears, essentially building a frequency table of all the different file types.
explanations.20: We're iterating through the Counter results, which gives us each unique extension and how many files have that extension.
explanations.21: This cleans up the extension for display—if it starts with a dot, remove the dot and make it uppercase (so '.py' becomes 'PY'), otherwise use it as-is.
